Graphs on the axes

The first four metrics are computed from the profiles φ(G) = (α(T,G)/e(T))T over the 85 test graphs, so they work for every graph: Euclidean distance E, the largest single-test difference E∞, the weighted sum ℓ1, and the Färnqvist–Jonsson–Thapper metric (Hilbert projective metric on the kept fractions 1 − φ). dist and d* need α between the graphs themselves and are available only for the 85 test cores.

Every axis lists the graphs themselves, in a chosen order. Matrix: graph G on x, graph H on y, colour = d(G,H). Surface: the same with height z = d(G,H). Triangle cube: graphs G, H, K on x, y, z; a point marks a triple where d(G,K) > d(G,H) + d(H,K), i.e. the triangle inequality fails, coloured by how much. For a metric the cube is empty.
